blocks.text: Give the caller an order cost it can use again.
return expression ends the current call and supplies the expression’s value to the caller.
result = function(arguments) stores the returned value.
Reaching the function’s end without return, or using return with no expression, returns None.
print displays values; it does not supply the function’s calculated return result.
Trace the product through return into cost, then into the caller’s addition. Contrast that with a helper that only prints the product: displaying it does not return it.
A display-only helper reaches its end and returns None. A missing return does not return the last calculation.

segments.label: Return calculated areas, store them, and combine them
segments.summary: An area function initially displays length multiplied by width. Although the apartment and yard areas appear on screen, those displayed numbers are not supplied as calculated results for the caller to combine. Changing the function to return length * width lets the caller store the results in house and yard, then add them to obtain 3,500 square feet. Return also stops the current function call: a display instruction placed after it is never reached. Moving that instruction before return allows the function to display the area and still supply its calculated value to the caller.

blocks.group_title: Return a value the caller can reuse

bridge.before: Watch how returning an area lets the caller store and reuse it, unlike displaying it. Notice why an instruction after return is never reached.
bridge.after: The clip connects returning, storing, and reusing values. It does not explain falling through or return without an expression; the text covers how both produce None.
